Yes, in my opinion it is.

Most of the chapter texts are leftovers from v4.0.3 and it is good to just ignore them at the moment.

It can fit to different places. From the word "authentication" it belongs to V2, from the word "service" it belong to V14. I prefer to keep V2 for "user authentication". The same way is done with authorization, we don't have service authorization requirements in V4, we have them in V14.

Yes, in my opinion it is.

It can fit to different places. From the word "authentication" it belongs to V2, from the word "service" it belong to V14. I prefer to keep V2 for "user authentication". The same way is done with authorization, we don't have service authentication requirements in V4, we have them in V14.

I like the list from 2.10.4 that carries attention to widespread mistakes:
>  Verify passwords, integrations with databases and third-party systems, seeds and internal secrets, and API keys ...

I think the current abstract "service accounts or 3rd party application credentials" does not cover all that.

---

> Secrets must not be included in the source code or stored within source code repositories.

I think "stored within source code repositories" is just a duplicate for the 1st part here.

I have seen too many times, that 3rd party integration secrets are stored as plain-text to a database and managed via user-interface. So I would like to get special attention for this one.
